title: Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan Benefit Terms for Employers: Participation and Application Limits
content:
The Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan is a benefit a worker reaches through their employer. These terms list, for every tier, the figures that concern the employer's program and how often a worker may borrow.

| Term | Paystride Payroll Loan 500 | Paystride Payroll Loan 1000 | Paystride Payroll Loan 2000 | Paystride Payroll Loan 3000 | Paystride Payroll Loan 4000 | Paystride Payroll Loan 5000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Months the employer's Earned Wage Access program must have been live | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Employer must have opted in to the loan benefit | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Loans in repayment allowed at once | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Calendar days after a decline before reapplying | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |
| Calendar days after payoff before a new loan may be applied for | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| An open loan may be refinanced into a new one | No | No | No | No | No | No |

**Employer program.** In every tier the employer's Earned Wage Access program must have been live for 3 months, and the employer must have opted in to the loan benefit.

**Number of loans.** In every tier 1 loan in repayment is allowed at once.

**After a decline.** In every tier 60 calendar days apply after a decline before reapplying.

**After a payoff.** In every tier the figure is 0 calendar days: no waiting period runs between the payoff of a loan and an application for a new one.

**Refinancing.** In no tier may an open loan be refinanced into a new one.

Hypothetical illustrations:

- An employer whose Earned Wage Access program went live 5 months ago has passed the 3-month figure; one live for 2 months has not.
- A worker whose previous loan was paid off this morning faces 0 days of waiting under the payoff figure.
